quotes.text: "If she is here alone without a husband or friends, it wouldn't be amiss to make her acquaintance,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And I have already dragged out a fortnight here."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Time goes fast, and yet it is so dull here!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "That's only the fashion to say it is dull here. A provincial will live in Belyov or Zhidra and not be dull, and when he comes here it's 'Oh, the dulness! Oh, the dust!' One would think he came from Grenada."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Where shall we go now? Shall we drive somewhere?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What different people one meets in the world!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You will be the first to despise me now."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You don't know what you are saying."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You seem to feel you need to be forgiven."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Forgiven? No. I am a bad, low woman; I despise myself and don't attempt to justify myself. It's not my husband but myself I have deceived. And not only just now; I have been deceiving myself for a long time. My husband may be a good, honest man, but he is a flunkey! I don't know what he does there, what his work is, but I know he is a flunkey! I was twenty when I was married to him. I have been tormented by curiosity; I wanted something better. 'There must be a different sort of life,' I said to myself. I wanted to live! To live, to live! . . . I was fired by curiosity . . . you don't understand it, but, I swear to God, I could not control myself; something happened to me: I could not be restrained. I told my husband I was ill, and came here. . . . And here I have been walking about as though I were dazed, like a mad creature; . . . and now I have become a vulgar, contemptible woman whom any one may despise."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Believe me, believe me, I beseech you . . ."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I love a pure, honest life, and sin is loathsome to me. I don't know what I am doing. Some people say: 'The Evil One has beguiled me.' And I may say of myself now that the Evil One has beguiled me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I found out your surname in the hall just now: it was written on the board-- Von Diderits,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No; I believe his grandfather was a German, but he is an Orthodox Russian himself."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's a good thing I am going away,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let me look at you once more . . . look at you once again. That's right."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I shall remember you . . . think of you,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "God be with you; be happy. Don't remember evil against me. We are parting forever --it must be so, for we ought never to have met. Well, God be with you."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's time for me to go north,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "The part of a lady-killer does not suit you at all, Dimitri."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "If only you knew what a fascinating woman I made the acquaintance of in Yalta!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You were right this evening: the sturgeon was a bit too strong!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "One would run away from a fence like that,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Here I've had a good sleep for some reason. What shall I do in the night?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "So much for the lady with the dog. . . so much for the adventure . . . . You're in a nice fix. . . ."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's quite possible she may go to the first performance,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, heavens! Why are these people here and this orchestra! . . ."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, how you have frightened me! I am half dead. Why have you come? Why?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I have thought of nothing but you all the time; I live only in the thought of you. And I wanted to forget, to forget you; but why, oh, why, have you come?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What are you doing, what are you doing!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "We are mad. Go away to-day; go away at once. . . . I beseech you by all that is sacred, I implore you. . . . There are people coming this way!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Do you hear, Dmitri Dmitritch? I will come and see you in Moscow. I have never been happy; I am miserable now, and I never, never shall be happy, never! Don't make me suffer still more! I swear I'll come to Moscow. But now let us part. My precious, good, dear one, we must part!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's three degrees above freezing-point, and yet it is snowing,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "The thaw is only on the surface of the earth; there is quite a different temperature at a greater height in the atmosphere."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And why are there no thunderstorms in the winter, father?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, how are you getting on there?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Wait; I'll tell you directly. . . . I can't talk."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Let her have her cry out. I'll sit down and wait,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You've had your cry; that's enough. . . . Let us talk now, let us think of some plan."
quotes.speaker: Unknown
